#871. Anne Hathaway Gives Birth, Welcomes Baby No. 3 With Adam Shulman

Anne Hathaway gave birth to her and husband Adam Shulman's third baby together, according to multiple outlets. The couple—who married in 2012—are already parents to sons Jonathan, 10, and Jack, 6.

Anne Hathaway has some news that will thrill you.

The Devil Wears Prada star gave birth to her third child with husband Adam Shulman, according to multiple outlets, with TMZ sharing photos of the actress walking around New York City with the newborn.

While Hathaway or Shulman—already parents to sons Jonathan, 10, and Jack, 6—haven't spoken publicly about welcoming their newest little one, they are more than prepared to take on their new roles as parents of three.

"The thing that to remember about boys is they have feelings," Hathaway—who tied the knot with Shulman in 2012—told Access Hollywood in July. "Sometimes, we think about that more in the realm of girls, but it's just as important to give boys that emotional foundation and make sure they feel just as safe as as we make our girls feel."

The Oscar winner first announced her pregnancy in June, sharing a video set to "Baby, I'm Yours" by Barbara Lewis in which she was seen cradling her growing baby bump in a flowing white dress.

She continued to bare her belly during the press tour for The Odyssey, most notably wearing a red, long-sleeved peplum jumpsuit by Ashlyn New York backwards by mistake.

"I did?" Hathaway quipped in a July 1 TikTok, after man fans pointed out that the one-piece looked different on the model who wore the jumpsuit during the label's Spring/Summer 2026 fashion show. "I did. I did."

But in Hathaway's defense, she's not the first pregnant star to tweak an outfit around her baby belly.

"I've heard from other pregnant women that the maternity hack is if you have to go to an event, you get a dress that has a train," she explained to Access Hollywood later that month, "and then you wear the train backwards and the train accommodates for the bump."

Plus, the Princess Diaries alum considered her baby bump to be the best fashion accessory. As she told E! News at the New York premiere of The Odyssey on July 14, "Cannot be beat."

"This is a lovely microphone,” Hathaway said while cradling her belly on the red carpet, “but I prefer my accessory.”

Besides, her pregnancy was an overall lovely surprise.

"It’s amazing," Hathway shared during a July 14 appearance on Late Night with Seth Meyers, before joking that she and Shulman—who she married in 2012—"knew what we were doing, but we were so shocked it worked."

"We were so shocked it went this way," she continued, "so we’re calling this one our buzzer-beater.”

Read on for more insight into Hathaway's motherhood journey, in her own words.

Anne Hathaway shared the special and exciting news that she and her hubby are having another baby! "It's not for a movie...⁣⁣#2," she wrote on Instagram, showing off her bump. "All kidding aside, for everyone going through infertility and conception hell, please know it was not a straight line to either of my pregnancies. Sending you extra love."

"They get down on the child's level and speak to them eye-to-eye to make their child feel empowered," she told The Sunday Times. "I thought that was really cool. I started doing that with Jonathan."

"I hadn't planned on ever confirming it and then I just, I had seen a photographer while I was on vacation, taking a photo, and I just thought, 'It's such a joyful and a sacred experience, you know, carrying life,'" Hathaway explained to E! News. "And I just thought, 'I don't want the first version of this to be out there with me covering or scowling at someone.'"

She told E! News that getting sleep has been challenging. "Honestly, I haven't slept in eight weeks. I have no idea what I'm saying," the actress jokingly stated. "This is probably going to go down as not the most normal interview on E! News."

"I'm going to stop drinking while my son is in my house just because I don't totally love the way I do it," Hathaway admitted to Ellen DeGeneres on her talk show. "He's getting to an age where he really does need me all the time in the mornings. I did one school run one day where I dropped him off at school, I wasn't driving, but I was hungover, and that was enough for me. I didn't love that one."

"The kind of mother I'll be depends on the kind of children I have," the Ocean's 8 actress shared with Vogue about the ultimate role she has as a mother.

"I can't believe we don't already have it," she shared with Elle magazine, further explaining that "We're encouraged to judge each other, but we should be turning our focus to the people and institutions who should be supporting us and currently aren't."

"I'm not perfect, but if I'm frustrated or distracted, I'm good at making sure he's safe and walking away, calming down and then coming back to him," she explained to The Sunday Times. She said "telling that harsh voice to be quiet" is one hard about motherhood. "I fall short every day, but I'm not going to beat myself up about it, I'm going to learn from it."

"I'm sorry. I am a new mother and I didn't time the feeding schedule—well, like I have any control over it," Hathaway said on Good Morning America with a laugh as she does press for the Alice Through the Looking Glass. "My kid was hungry, I had to feed him, I missed the first 20 minutes so I can't tell you about the beginning of the movie."

"When [my son] Johnny was a week old and I was holding him and I was in the ninth level of ecstasy, I just all of a sudden thought, 'Mommy guilt is invented nonsense,'" she told Elle magazine.

#870. Romario demands Ancelotti sacking as war of words continues

Few would have predicted that Carlo Ancelotti would be facing the wrath of a Brazil legend just 18 months into his tenure as head coach of the national team.

But Romario, Brazil's fourth-highest scorer behind only Neymar, Pele and Ronaldo, has publicly demanded legendary manager Ancelotti be relieved of his duties twice in the past week.

It all started after Brazil suffered a 3-2 friendly defeat by Japan on Friday thanks to a controversial stoppage-time winner from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto.

Ancelotti received a red card for dissent in the aftermath - the first of his international management career, as Barcelona forward Raphinha also saw red.

And after Brazil's friendly defeat, Romario took to social media to air his frustrations about the former Real Madrid boss.

"Ancelotti, enough is enough! Pack your bags and leave!" he wrote on Instagram.

"Nobody questions your history. You are one of the greatest coaches world football has ever seen, but that was at club level."

Brazil were eliminated by Norway in the last 16 at the 2026 World Cup, meaning they failed to qualify for the quarter-finals for the first time since 1990.

And Romario alluded to this too, stating the country "can't take the risk of throwing another World Cup in the trash - the time to act is now!"

The Brazil boss has been in the game long enough to know how to deal with all sorts of opinions.

Ancelotti has won the Champions League a record five times as a head coach and won the league title in all of Europe's top five divisions, along with multiple domestic cups.

But his record with Brazil is far from perfect. Across 21 matches, they have recorded 12 wins, four draws and five defeats.

However, while Ancelotti acknowledges the need for improvement, he emphasised the fact that it is still "a new project".

Speaking before Brazil's friendly with Singapore on Tuesday the Italian said: "In a democratic country with freedom of speech, everyone is allowed to express their opinion.

"It's not up to me to say whether the things he says are correct, wrong or just stupid. The truth is that Romario talks a lot. A lot. It's his right."

Despite the criticism he has faced, Ancelotti feels Brazil are on the right track - and who is to tell him otherwise when you look at his track record?

"I really like what we're doing," he said.

You would have thought that would have been enough to let it lie for the time being.

But before Brazil had even kicked a ball in their next friendly against Singapore, Romario was speaking out again.

The former striker, who is the ninth-highest scorer in football history with 784 goals, doubled down on his calls for Ancelotti to be sacked.

"I talk a lot because when it comes to the national team, I have size, weight and power of speech," Romario, 60, said.

"I do not speak to gain followers, I do not speak for people to like me. I speak my mind.

"I have worn this shirt for many years and I am pretty sure I was one of the ones that helped the 'little yellow' be respected all over the world."

He said he respected Ancelotti but added he hadn't "added anything new" to the national side.

"I will say it again: resign! We will find another coach who will do a better job than you.

"And I'm saying this to your face, not through a message, including to the president of the [Brazilian Football Confederation], who is long overdue to fire you."

Brazil faced Singapore in their final match of 2026 on Tuesday and won 7-0.

Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior, who has come under scrutiny of his own so far this season, scored a hat-trick within the opening 21 minutes while Bournemouth winger Rayan and Chelsea's Estevao were also on the scoresheet.

That result that may bring a pause to proceedings in this war of words for now.

However, if this past seven days has proved anything, it is that this saga is likely far from over.

#869. Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared

The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer

Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons

Key ins: Bruno Guimarães (Newcastle, £75m), Ezri Konsa (Aston Villa, £51m), Piero Hincapié (Bayer Leverkusen, £45m), Christos Tzolis (Club Brugge, £34m)

Key outs: Leandro Trossard (Besiktas, £15.3m), Jakub Kiwior (Porto, £14.5m), Gabriel Jesus (Barcelona, £8.6m), Fábio Vieira (Hamburg, £7.7m), Christian Nørgaard (Everton, £7m), Ethan Nwaneri (Borussia Dortmund, loan)

It is all change at Villa and, although a little trepidation is inevitable, a refresh was probably overdue. At the same time, Unai Emery did not want to lose so many key players and Villa’s manager has made clear there is no such thing as a transition season in his eyes. Villa have generated about £300m from the sales of nine players and brought in 10 at a cost of about £250m. Villa have lowered their wage bill and changed the profile of their squad. Zion Suzuki, Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi, names on the lips of Villa’s rivals, are particularly exciting signings. Last summer there was concern Villa had gone stale and 12 months ago they ended up fretting on deadline day – Harvey Elliott and Jadon Sancho joined on loan – but there was no such chaos this time. Ben Fisher

Key ins: Johan Manzambi (Freiburg, £51m), Nicolas Jackson (Chelsea, £47.5m), Ibrahim Mbaye (PSG, £47m), João Gomes (Wolves, £34m), Zion Suzuki (Parma, £30m), Taylor Harwood-Bellis (Southampton, £25m), Matteo Ruggeri (Atlético Madrid, £21.4m), Leon Goretzka (Bayern Munich, free), Aaron Wan-Bissaka (West Ham, loan), Alejandro Garnacho (Chelsea, loan)

Key outs: Morgan Rogers (Chelsea, £117m), Ollie Watkins (Al-Hilal, £51m), Ezri Konsa (Arsenal, £51m), Youri Tielemans (Manchester United, £35m), Donyell Malen (Roma, £21.6m), Lewis Dobbin (Southampton, £9m), Lucas Digne (PSG, £8.5m), Emiliano Martínez (Chelsea, £7.5m), Evann Guessand (Crystal Palace, loan)

The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?

Perhaps Bournemouth’s best business was keeping hold of their coveted key players, chiefly Eli Junior Kroupi, Rayan, Alex Scott and Tyler Adams. Bournemouth rejected bids from Chelsea for Scott and stayed true to their plan of resisting offers to give Marco Rose the best chance of succeeding, with the club attempting to juggle European competition and the league for the first time. The arrival of the Portugal centre-back António Silva, 22, from Benfica looks a typically smart replacement for Marcos Senesi, 29. Kroupi’s freak foot injury, which will probably keep him out until November, may have proved a blessing in disguise in terms of retaining the 20-year-old. BF

Avoiding a repeat of last year’s upheaval was a major boost. Keith Andrews held on to his best players and made smart additions to a solid squad. Mamadou Sangaré has added quality in midfield since joining from Lens and looks the bargain of the summer. Callum Wilson has brought experience up front after signing on a free and Jaidon Anthony provides cover on the flanks after his £15m move from Burnley. El Hadji-Malick Diouf, signed from West Ham, offers potential at left-back. Jacob Steinberg

Key ins: Mamadou Sangaré (Lens, £39m), El Hadji Malick Diouf (West Ham, £35m), Jaidon Anthony (Burnley, £15m), Jannik Schuster (Red Bull Salzburg, £14m), Callum Wilson (West Ham, free)

Key outs: Ethan Pinnock (Coventry, £6m), Jordan Henderson (Chelsea, free)

Deadline day deals to bring in the exciting Nigeria forward Femi Azeez from Millwall and the Spanish midfielder Chema Andrés from Stuttgart made it 12 signings in another summer of transition, Azeez’s arrival being announced almost 12 hours after the window shut. The departures of Jan Paul van Hecke, Carlos Baleba and Carl Rushworth brought in more than £140m as the Brighton model continues to deliver big profits, although losing last season’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, to Chelsea for a mere £5m may be the biggest loss if the new striker Promise David cannot bring the goals. EA

Xabi Alonso’s appointment as manager was the biggest signing of the summer. Chelsea have been sensible since turning to the Spaniard. Morgan Rogers has started well after joining for £117m. Maxence Lacroix adds power in defence, Marco Palestra versatility on the flanks. Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson can raise standards in the dressing room. But there was the usual revolving door. Money was made on a host of outgoings. Marc Cucurella, one of the world’s best left-backs and sold to Real Madrid, looks a bigger loss than Enzo Fernández. However a worry is that Chelsea did not replace Fernández after selling him to Manchester City for £125m, their late £47m move for Monaco’s Lamine Camara collapsing at the last. JS

It remains to be seen whether Coventry have struck the right balance in the market. Frank Lampard wanted to maintain momentum but add power and physicality. Coventry also sought to address their lack of Premier League experience with Taiwo Awoniyi and Ethan Pinnock. Coventry were the highest scorers in English football’s top four tiers last season but the step up means the pressure is on Awoniyi, never prolific for Nottingham Forest, Sidiki Cherif, a promising 19-year-old, and Ellis Simms to deliver before Haji Wright returns from injury. Stephen Mfuni, a teenage loanee from Manchester City and their 11th and final summer signing, increases their left-back options. BF

The lost tug of war with Sunderland over Malick Fofana summed up another chaotic deadline day for Palace, who were still scrambling for signings in the final minutes and confirmed the arrivals of Ben Chilwell, Quinten Timber and Darío Osorio after the window shut. The new manager, Pierre Sage, will at least be pleased to have secured more defensive reinforcements after losing Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea, with the loanees Honest Ahanor and Axel Disasi adding much-needed depth. Palace also kept hold of Ismaïla Sarr – presuming he doesn’t join a club in Saudi Arabia before the Sunday deadline there – after rejecting an approach from Liverpool for the Senegal forward. EA

It was a window that revealed the extent of The Friedkin Group’s ambitions, the strength of the club’s finances after the move to a new stadium, the state of the relationship between the manager and chief executive and the expertise of the senior leadership team; and none of it was positive. The owners deserve some credit for listening to fans and halting the self-defeating sale of Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest but otherwise it was a modest window that descended into a shambles. The club’s best player was sold for a below-market fee, a move for Folarin Balogun collapsed and although the equally desperate search for a right-back ended with Ainsley Maitland-Niles signing, David Moyes was left with one striker and a smaller squad than he started the day with, despite repeatedly urging his employers to strengthen. AH

It was a summer of change at Craven Cottage. Marco Silva departed after five successful years in charge and was replaced by the inexperienced Álvaro Arbeloa, who has focused on adding youth. Gonzalo García, César Palacios and Manuel Ángel followed Arbeloa from Real Madrid and Shea Charles is an exciting signing from Southampton. Some stalwarts have left. Raúl Jiménez joined Wolves and Harry Wilson went to Leeds. Fulham looked to strengthen. They secured the midfielder Hugo Larsson and centre-back David Affengruber on deadline day but missed out on another target, the right-back Andrei Ratiu. JS

“Think of us like a volcano,” said Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali, in early July. “It’s boiling right now and it’s going to erupt.” Two months on the Ilicali has presided over 18 signings, investing more than £150m and his manager, Sergej Jakirovic, has choreographed two Premier League wins. The horizon looks infinitely brighter than in June, when the playoff winners sold two players for a combined £8.5m to avoid breaching English Football League spending rules and a near-certain six-point deduction. Hull, remember, spent last season under a two-window EFL transfer embargo. They have compensated for that this summer and, although time will tell whether all those new faces are compatible, reasons for optimism remain real. Not least because last season’s cult hero loanee forward Joe Gelhardt has signed permanently from Leeds. Louise Taylor

#867. Millwall open disciplinary proceedings against Baker

Baker featured in five Premier League games for Brighton in the 2023-24 season

Millwall are undertaking disciplinary proceedings against forward Benicio Baker following social media posts critical of senior figures at the club, BBC Sport understands.

The 22-year-old winger has played only for the Lions' under-21 side since joining from Brighton in February 2025 on a long-term deal.

BBC Sport understands the proceedings relate to a number of off-field matters, including social media activity.

Posts attributed to Baker's account, which has since been deactivated on Instagram but has been widely republished, appeared critical of senior figures at Millwall and suggested he "can't even train with the (under) 21s".

It is understood Baker was initially unavailable because of injury, but he is now the subject of disciplinary proceedings which, in the most serious circumstances, could lead to the cancellation of his contract.

Baker is also understood to be exploring options away from Millwall.

At the height of his career, Baker made six first-team appearances for Brighton under former manager Roberto de Zerbi, including in the Premier League.

The England Under-20 international also spent time in the academy systems at West Ham and Porto before making 14 senior appearances on loan as Port Vale finished second in League Two in 2024.

While at West Ham, before joining Porto, he was linked with moves to overseas clubs including Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Benfica.

Millwall have declined to comment, while representatives for Baker have been contacted.

#866. Why Leonardo DiCaprio Didn’t Return for Brad Pitt’s Cliff Booth Movie

Brad Pitt shared the real reason why his Once Upon a Time in Hollywood costar Leonardo DiCaprio isn't in the sequel, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth: "It just seemed like a big ask."

Leonardo DiCaprio is missing out on The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.

Though Oscar winner starred in 2019's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, he opted not to appear in the Quentin Tarantino movie's upcoming sequel due to time constraints, according to his former costar Brad Pitt.

"It would have been great fun, but it required a lot of prosthetics, which is a good couple of weeks prepping to get him," Pitt told The Hollywood Reporter Nov. 16, referencing how the follow-up's trailer teased that DiCaprio's Rick Dalton had become "too fat" for his titular stuntman to serve as a body double. "It’s hardly worth the cost for a cameo."

"It was talked about for a while, but it just seemed like a big ask," the 62-year-old explained, adding that DiCaprio's character does get a few "sweet tributes" in the movie.

But the Titanic alum wasn't the only notable name who declined to return for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. After all, David Fincher stepped in to take the directing reins from Tarantino, who opted to only write the script of the new installment.

"I don’t bemoan that all because it’s such a commitment, especially for a director," Pitt shared. “Things sat around for about nine months and Fincher and I were talking about doing something again, and it just happened."

As for DiCaprio's thoughts on the new movie?

"Ultimately, I cannot wait to see the Cliff Booth story," he told Deadline last year. "I think David Fincher’s the perfect man for the job. Quentin is a huge fan of his work, I’m a huge fan of his work, and there’s nobody better to carry on that lineage and tell that story."

DiCaprio added, "It’s the next phase of Cliff Booth’s life. I’m excited to see it."

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth premieres in IMAX Nov. 25 and on Netflix Dec. 23. For more movies hitting the big screen soon, keep reading...

#864. Swansea boss Matos on brink of Strasbourg move

Swansea boss Vitor Matos spent five years on Jurgen Klopp's staff at Liverpool

Vitor Matos is on the brink of leaving Swansea City to take charge of French top-flight club Strasbourg.

Matos, 38, is understood to have said goodbye to players and staff at the Swans' Fairwood training base on Tuesday after Strasbourg made an official approach for the Swansea head coach.

There is no confirmation yet that a deal has been agreed between the clubs, but Strasbourg are thought to be ready to pay in the region of Â£5m to secure the Portuguese's services.

News of Strasbourg's interest had emerged on Monday, with Matos - who is under contract at Swansea until 2030 - telling the Championship club he wanted to leave.

Four members of Matos' coaching team - Diogo Medeiros, Toze Mendes, Goncalo Ricca and head of goalkeeping Pedro Pereira - are also expected to depart.

That will leave Swansea stalwarts Leon Britton and Kristian O'Leary as the only remaining senior staff members at the club heading into Saturday's home game against West Bromwich Albion.

Matos had been due to celebrate a year in charge at Swansea later this month.

Current Strasbourg boss Hugo Oliveira, Matos' fellow countryman, has been under pressure after a run of five defeats in six matches.

Oliveira has managed only three wins in 10 league games since succeeding Gary O'Neil - who left to take over at Ipswich Town â in July.

O'Neil led Strasbourg to an eighth-place finish last season, but they are currently 13th in Ligue 1, only two points above the relegation zone.

Strasbourg are a sister club of Premier League side Chelsea.

Matos has turned Swansea from potential relegation contenders to promotion hopefuls since taking charge, with the club 20th in the Championship when he took over last November.

The Swans finished 11th last season and have made further strides in the first third of this campaign.

Vitor Matos led Swansea to seven wins in their first 10 league games of the season, though they have since lost four in five

Matos' team have been among the early-season pacesetters in the second tier, enjoying two spells on top of the table, but their form has dipped in recent weeks.

Swansea have suffered four defeats in their past five matches, though they remain only three points off top spot before West Brom's visit.

Matos was touted as a contender to take charge at Crystal Palace earlier this season - the Eagles have since appointed Thomas Frank - while he has also been linked with a return to Portugal on the back of his impact at Swansea.

When asked in October about the Palace links, Matos said: "I'm Swansea manager. I love being here, love my players, love the staff, so my focus is always on the next game and what we can do better."

In an interview last week, Swansea chief executive Tom Gorringe acknowledged that Matos' impact will not have gone unnoticed at other clubs, though he played down the idea of the former Liverpool coach having his head turned.

"The reality is there'll always be interest in anyone performing well in any role on and off the pitch," Gorringe said.

"That's one of the outcomes of being successful - we're aware of that.

"[But] we're all quite happy. We've all agreed to go on this journey together and we hope that Vitor is here a long time."

After meeting West Brom, who are fifth in the second tier, sixth-placed Swansea go to second-placed Middlesbrough next Tuesday.

They then host Cardiff City in the first south Wales derby in two seasons on Sunday, 29 November.

Vitor Matos latest: Strasbourg close in on Swansea head coach

Vitor Matos is relatively inexperienced if you look at his senior management experience alone, but his wealth of footballing experience is evident when taking a wider look at his footballing journey.

Speaking to BBC Sport earlier this season, Matos explained how his 23 years in football have informed his development - a journey that began when a 15-year-old Matos was inspired by Jose Mourinho's Champions League triumph with Porto.

So, although he only took his first managerial job at the start of last season in the second division of Portugal, to call Matos an overnight success story would be false.

He developed an understanding of positional play while working as a youth coach at FC Porto, before moving to China. As technical director and an under-16 coach of Shandong Taishan, he added layers of knowledge to his positional game:

"In China, I understood that to arrive at a more positional game, you could have different steps beforehand," he explained.

"There is a benefit to having more players close to each other, rather than spreading them over space.

"If you spread them over space, you are demanding that, technically, they can solve many situations one-v-one. If they come closer to the ball, you can generate more possibilities. You can create a tempo that allows other players to be better in the big spaces."

The uniqueness of these overloads, around the ball, have been a hallmark of some of Swansea's impressive attacking play this season.

Following stints in Portugal and China, he then found himself working alongside Jurgen Klopp and Pep Lijnders at Liverpool, which provided him a greater understanding of senior football at the elite level.

"Liverpool influenced me a lot in terms of counter-pressing, pressing, intensity, and what makes you grow as a team," he said.

"The most important thing is how much you believe in your idea, and this style is how I see football. That's why I want this to be the foundation for our team."

#862. Blake Shelton Shares Best Part of Being Stepdad to Gwen Stefani’s Kids

Blake Shelton revealed what he loves most about being a stepdad to Gwen Stefani's kids Kingston, 20, Zuma, 18, and Apollo, 12, sharing how they spend most afternoons.

Blake Shelton has taken to fatherhood like a honey bee to a honeysuckle.

The “God’s Country” singer shared what one of his favorite parts of parenthood is after becoming stepdad to wife Gwen Stefani’s kids with ex-husband Gavin Rossdale: Kingston, 20, Zuma, 18, and Apollo, 12.

“The most cliche dad thing I do every single day when the kids get home from school, Apollo—our youngest—we throw the football for about 30 minutes,” Shelton told Taste of Country in a clip posted to Instagram Nov. 15. “He’s got this thing, he loves to jump on the trampoline while I throw the football to him, so he can do the crazy Odell Beckham catches, DeAndre Hopkins stuff.”

And while the 50-year-old is happy Apollo is able to get his energy out, Shelton is keeping his feet firmly planted on the ground, quipping, “Just throwing the ball wears me out.”

Thankfully, he and Zuma enjoy a less strenuous activity, as Shelton shared that he and the teen spend time playing the guitar together.

“It’s not me showing him stuff,” the Grammy nominee added. “It's him showing me stuff. ‘Have you heard this song?’ ‘You heard of this artist?’ ‘Listen to this song.’”

The duo share musical moments “almost every single day,” and that along with Apollo’s football antics are just a few of the memories Shelton values as their stepdad.

“I love it,” he said. “I can't wait ’til they get home.”

The “Sangria” singer has also been there to support Stefani’s eldest son Kingston with his musical career, as the couple attended his concert at the Troubadour in Los Angeles Nov. 10, alongside Stefani’s ex Rossdale.

Since tying the knot with Stefani in 2021, Shelton has been candid about how his life has found new fulfillment as a stepdad.

"I didn't know what I was signing up for, but I was all about signing up for it," Shelton said during the 2022 Country Radio Seminar. "And every day I've fallen in love with the boys as much as I do with Gwen."

Keep reading for the hella good deep dive into the love story between Shelton and Stefani.

"I think he's hot, don't you? But to be super honest, it is kind of crazy we both went through the same thing at the same time. There's been so many people that I've gotten so much comfort from. Just people coming to me and telling me their story. Not confiding, but sharing, which has just helped me see things from a different perspective and move forward." —Gwen to Ryan Seacrest in November 2015

"How can I not be [in love]? She is the greatest. She is the greatest." —Blake on Today in March 2018.

"When you have a broken heart—at least, when I do—you got to get it out of your system. You want people to sympathize with you. I was at rock bottom, in the middle of hell...Gwen saved my life. Who else on earth could understand going through a high-profile divorce from another musician?" —Blake to Billboard in July 2016

"I grew up in Orange County, so I don't know if you've been down there, but it's nothing like the middle of America and our nature was the beach. So to be able to be in Oklahoma and be able to experience a ranch kind of vibe is just something I never ever had, so it's just been really, it's been great, amazing." —Gwen on Jimmy Kimmel Live in August 2020

#860. Almost impossible for Scotland to not qualify for Euro 2028... or is it?

The statement is enough to make any Scotland fan uncomfortable, but that's been the relaxed theme going into this Nations League campaign among some outside of Hampden.

Euro 2028 has various different access routes, especially for the host nations of England, Republic of Ireland, Scotland and Wales, who even have two spare spaces between them secured before a ball is kicked.

But, in the bleak, barren and grim aftermath of Scotland's 4-0 scudding by Switzerland in St Gallen, "almost impossible" almost feels like a challenge.

Scotland began with three shots at reaching the finals, where they would play at Hampden Park if they made it. We're now down to two.

They could have qualified for the Euro 2028 finals with help from the Nations League. Not straightforward, but absolutely achievable.

Finish top of group B1 containing Switzerland, Slovenia and North Macedonia, then prevail in the play-off.

In Sebastien Pocognoli's first six games in charge, he failed to deliver that, his new-look squad and system only offering seven points.

Not only that but that third-place finish has further repercussions.

Scotland's next route lies in the Euro qualifiers, with the draw taking place in Belfast on 6 December. Can't wait.

Pocognoli's team will go into pot three for that, making a shot at progression that much more difficult.

That means the Scots could be drawn in a group with the likes of Serbia, Turkey, Czech Republic, Switzerland, or Austria as their pot 2 opponent.

For example, Scotland could be in a group with Spain, Switzerland, Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan. Please, no.

The top 12 group winners and the eight best runners-up go straight through, with the rest of the runners-up going into a play-off with the best Nations League non-qualified group winners.

If Scotland make a hash of that, then do not fear...

Uefa is reserving two spots for the two best-ranked host nations who have not qualified after the completion of the qualifying group stage.

It's now feasible this may come into play.

Going on the assumption England - who have just turned over world champions Spain - will qualify, that leaves Scotland, Wales and Ireland. Despite the qualifying draw being in Belfast, Northern Ireland aren't a host nation.

If one of them qualifies through other means, then happy days.

If they do not, then the Scots will need to hope they are not the lowest-ranked team among the three or they face being locked out of their own house party.

#859. WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?

Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw

Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Suzanne Wrack

Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City

Manchester United earned their fourth clean sheet in all competitions in their 2-0 defeat of Crystal Palace. Maya Le Tissier stole the headlines with her goal on her 150th appearance for the club but the team’s improved defensive stability is also catching the eye and the centre-back is key to that. “For a defender you expect as the minimum you need to defend well and help to build,” said the head coach, Eva Olid. “But now she’s scoring goals and that is more than a manager can ask from a centre-back. She’s in a high level and I’m so happy for her.” Le Tissier is showing consistent solidity and appears to be enjoying life under Olid now that things have settled, after seven goals conceded in their opening two WSL games. United have conceded four in eight WSL games since and are starting to show their flair. SW

Have teams stopped fearing Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium? Their run of five consecutive WSL draws at home suggests so. London City Lionesses had 56% possession on Sunday and controlled the game for significant spells, especially in the second half, and although Arsenal created the greater chances, they do not play with the aura of a side attracting the largest attendances in the division. Renée Slegers was asked whether she was worried her team were losing that home “fear factor” and said: “No, because we love playing at the Emirates. We had the biggest crowd so far in the season, the atmosphere was fantastic under the lights.” Probed further about her side’s home form, the head coach said: “I don’t think we’ve lost the fear factor, I think it’s a very hard place for oppositions to come.” Her side host West Ham next Sunday, looking for that elusive home WSL win. Tom Garry

Tottenham Hotspur were the latest team frustrated by Everton’s defensive solidity as they were held to a goalless draw. Despite controlling the ball and registering 17 shots, only three efforts were on target as they failed to score for the first time. Martin Ho was keen to highlight their opponents’ strengths as a key reason. “When we got into that attacking third, it was going to take something really special,” he told Spursplay. “They defended so deep with so many numbers behind the ball. You’re waiting for one of those moments to drop.” It was just the kind of performance fans have come to expect from Scott Phelan’s side. Unbeaten in their past three, in which they have faced Manchester United, Chelsea and Spurs, Everton have developed a strong resilience and character in recent weeks. Where they struggle is at the other end. Everton have scored eight goals this season (three of them own goals), higher than only Charlton in the WSL. Sophie Downey

Liverpool ended their five-game winless league run with a statement victory over struggling Brighton, their third away win in 17 games. It has been a frustrating October and November block for Gareth Taylor and his team so there was much relief on the sideline that they were finally able to turn performance and opportunity into three points. Liverpool had less of the ball but their fast counterattacking proved too much for the Seagulls. A significant key to their success was Beata Olsson. She has six goals from her past five games in all competitions, stepping up when her team have needed it most. Injuries have kept out Aurélie Csillag and Ceri Holland for the best part of the season and Sophie Roman Haug is recovering from an anterior cruciate ligament injury sustained 13 months ago. With limited attacking options, therefore, it will be very welcome that the Swedish striker has found her form in front of goal. SD

Viviane Asseyi continued her impressive scoring form with a superb brace in West Ham’s 2-0 victory over Charlton, taking her WSL tally to seven this season. The striker opened the scoring with a composed finish from the edge of the area before producing the standout moment of the afternoon, curling a spectacular 25-yard free-kick into the top corner beyond Charlton’s goalkeeper, Anna Koivunen. Asseyi could have completed a hat-trick but her two goals proved decisive. West Ham’s head coach, Rita Guarino, described her as “an important player”, adding that Asseyi was in a good goalscoring spell. Guarino felt Asseyi could have been happier with a hat-trick, but her latest double underlines her importance to West Ham’s attacking threat. Mitul Samji

Poor officiating dominated the narrative of the second city derby as Aston Villa edged Birmingham City 1-0, with both sides feeling hard done by. First, City felt Lucy Parker had fouled Océane Hurtré in the penalty area in the 24th minute, only for the referee to award a corner. Whether the incident was inside the box was disputable, but it did appear to be a foul. Minutes later, Villa had a goal from Océane Deslandes overruled for what was declared a foul on the goalkeeper in another contentious call, but they managed to find a winner in the second half. The decisions added to growing concerns about consistency in the WSL. Ho recently suggested officiating had worsened, and matches such as this do little to ease those concerns. Before VAR is introduced, improving the quality of refereeing must be a priority to avoid undermining the league’s standards and progress. Réshma Rao

#858. Why always him? The rise and fall of Balotelli

Why always him? The rise and fall of Balotelli

Perhaps better known for off-field antics than his undeniable - yet arguably wasted - talent with the ball at his feet, the Italian has always attracted headlines.

Fifteen years have passed since his famous 'Why always me?' Manchester derby T-shirt celebration, which came just days after a firework was set off in his own bathroom, causing a house fire.

The 36-year-old is still playing, now in the United Arab Emirates first division with Al-Ittifaq alongside his biological brother, Enock Barwuah.

Here, BBC Sport looks at a career that has included 13 clubs, six countries - and an assist for arguably the most famous goal in Premier League history.

Typical of his unconventional footballing life, Balotelli's career did not begin in an elite club's academy.

Instead, by his mid-teens he was turning out for Italian third-tier side Lumezzane, close to the family home in Concesio.

A trial at Barcelona did not lead to a long-term stay, and instead he was picked up by Inter Milan in 2006.

It was at Inter that Balotelli first came across his great mentor - Roberto Mancini.

The relationship between the two has been likened to that of a father and son. Under the Italian coach's tutelage, Balotelli flourished.

Aged 17, Balotelli helped Inter win the 2007-08 Serie A title and reach the Coppa Italia final, memorably scoring twice against Juventus to send his side into the semi-finals.

Life changed for Balotelli with the arrival of Jose Mourinho in the weeks after that campaign ended.

There would be disagreements, disciplinary action and accusations that Balotelli's attitude was not up to scratch. Mourinho said Balotelli was "unmanageable" and described one performance as "close to a zero rating".

The relationship with Mourinho was fractious - a rare occasion when the Special One was confounded by a player.

Balotelli still won three Serie A titles and one Champions League with Inter, but his reputation as a supposed loose cannon was already beginning to overshadow his feats as a player.

Balotelli played for Mancini at Inter and Manchester City - and was briefly recalled for Italy by his old boss in 2018

Logic dictated that Balotelli's next step should be to reunite with mentor Mancini. That happened in August 2010 when the 20-year-old joined Manchester City.

Mancini set out to show that the unpredictable ways of Balotelli could be harnessed for the team's good, aiming to get more out of him than Mourinho could.

A hardline stance on discipline often appeared to soften when Mancini dealt with Balotelli, who by spring 2011 had garnered a reputation in England as a fantastic footballer who could not stay away from controversy.

Having already been sent off twice for City and been involved in a car crash - not in his famous camouflage Bentley but an Audi R8 - the striker threw a dart at a youth-team player, an act that showed a level of immaturity.

After helping City to win the FA Cup in 2011, ending their 35-year major trophy drought, Balotelli came under scrutiny after attempting a backheel trick shot when through on goal during a pre-season friendly against LA Galaxy.

Mancini swiftly hooked him, later questioning his mentality by saying: "If you are serious, you can play 90 minutes. If not, you can come and sit by me on the bench."

Sometimes the audacity paid off - like the famous shoulder goal and subsequent nonchalant celebration against Norwich.

In October 2011, emergency services attended his Cheshire home to deal with a firework lit in his bathroom. Balotelli said a friend had been responsible.

BBC Sport reported at the time that four firefighters used two hose reel water jets to douse the flames, with a large fan deployed to clear smoke.

Mario Balotelli scored 30 goals in 80 games for Manchester City

Days later he was in the spotlight for the right reasons as he scored City's opener in a 6-1 win over Manchester United, celebrating with the 'Why always me?' T-shirt.

There were other stories - that he had given a homeless person Â£1,000, that he had turned up to a young boy's school to confront the headmaster about the child being bullied, that he drove around Manchester handing out presents while dressed as Santa.

True? Perhaps only Balotelli knows and he has often denied such rumours. But such was his reputation at the time that the stories became plausible.

A chant City fans coined made reference to his ironic allergy to grass - which kept him out of a Europa League match in 2011 - and driving around Moss Side with "a wallet full of cash".

On the pitch, Balotelli was sent off against Arsenal in April 2012 in what, at the time, seemed like a season-defining moment that could end Manchester City's title bid.

But one month later he assisted Sergio Aguero's last-gasp goal against Queens Park Rangers that gave City a first Premier League title. It was his only Premier League assist that season.

Micah Richards, who was a team-mate and friend to Balotelli at City, said: "He was crazy in a good way. He was brilliant to have around the squad - a cult hero not just for the nonsense he did off the field but on it as well.

"The best thing about him is he's a lovely guy - he's not arrogant or how the papers try to perceive him, he's just a bit mad."

But did the moments of brilliance make the "nonsense" worth it?

Despite once insisting his patience with Balotelli was "limitless", Mancini ultimately had a rethink.

The final straw came in January 2013 when the pair had an argument at the training ground. Balotelli left for AC Milan later that month.

Mancini said: "He is not a bad guy, and a fantastic player, but I'm very sorry for him as he continues to lose his talent and his quality. I don't have any words for his behaviour.

"I hope for him he can understand he is in a bad way for his future."

Affection remained on both sides, but the relationship had become too fraught.

"Once upon a time, Mario did genuinely believe he was one of the best players in the world," said Nedum Onuoha, another former City team-mate.

"There are lots of stories about him from his time at City, but the one I remember is at our old training ground in Carrington when someone was talking about Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, and Mario said he was as good as them - and he was deadly serious.

"It obviously hasn't worked out that way, but he still has done so much more with his career than most players could even dream of."

'Why always me?' - relive that Balotelli moment in huge Man City win

'Balotelli to Barnsley? Now that is one Mario story I don't believe'

Balotelli never threatened to have an international career to rival Ronaldo or Messi.

But there were still moments that linger in the memory.

He became the first black player to feature for Italy at a major tournament when he starred at Euro 2012.

And, more than that, he hit three goals to finish as the tournament's joint top scorer - with five others - as Italy lost to Spain in the final.

An abiding image is that of a shirtless Balotelli flexing his muscles after scoring the goal that sent the Azzurri to the final, with a 2-1 win against Germany.

Balotelli's celebration against Germany in the Euro 2012 semi-finals became an iconic image of the tournament

Yet that tournament proved to be the peak of Balotelli's international career.

Italy's national team took a downward turn, and so too did his club career. By 2015, Balotelli had more or less became an Azzurri afterthought.

While Balotelli enjoyed some big moments in an Italy shirt, he did not always feel the love reciprocated from his country of birth.

Before Euro 2012 he threatened to leave the pitch if he was subjected to racist abuse and spoke openly about the vitriol he suffered while playing for Inter.

In fact, racist abuse has followed Balotelli throughout his career and he has commendably refused to tolerate it.

Born Mario Barwuah in Palermo to Ghanaian parents, Balotelli was placed into foster care aged three.

Initially, he stayed with his foster parents - Silvia and Francesco Balotelli - in Brescia during the week, then returned to his biological parents at weekends. He was eventually fostered on a full-time basis and took on the Balotelli surname.

Balotelli identifies with both parts of his heritage - Ghana and Italy - and he struggled to reconcile his love for a nation with the people who aimed verbal abuse his way.

The good times were all too brief: 36 caps and 14 goals has been his tally since 2018. He wanted more and has often made it known.

Onuoha said: "Playing for his country was always so important to him and that's another really positive thing about him, that he had that drive and ambition."

Mancini told AC Milan that Balotelli could become one of the world's best while in Serie A.

A glut of goals followed the striker's return to the San Siro in January 2013, before a surprising move back to the Premier League followed 18 months later.

Liverpool had been impressed, but Balotelli's spell on Merseyside would prove forgettable for all. One goal in 16 Premier League games under Brendan Rodgers was not what was expected from the Â£16m buy.

The failed transfer sparked a loan move back to Milan, where injuries hampered his progress. When it was time for Balotelli to return to Merseyside, Jurgen Klopp had arrived and said the striker would not be part of his Liverpool plans.

Balotelli later called the move to Anfield "the worst mistake of my life".

Steven Gerrard and Mario Balotelli were briefly Liverpool team-mates - but it didn't work out at Anfield for the Italian

Was it that Liverpool move that sent Balotelli's career spiralling into freefall?

Spells in Nice, Marseille, Brescia and Monza followed - each to varying degrees of success but never with a feeling of stability.

Then came Turkish club Adana Demirspor, Swiss outfit Sion and Italian side Genoa. He spent no more than one season at a time with any of these clubs, although he did return to Demirspor for a second stint.

And so to the present day, with Balotelli aged 36 and plying his trade in the UAE.

It is easy to wonder what might have been had Balotelli stayed in Manchester, had he managed to settle enough to entirely fulfil his potential.

But, after so much media attention and a career that has spanned more continents and leagues than most, it is perhaps also understandable that Balotelli has settled on fulfilment through simply playing the game he loves with his brother.

"Playing with a family member like he is will give him that happiness," said Onuoha.

"And yes, it is not Serie A, La Liga or the Premier League, but Mario is on a field sharing it with his brother - for him that will mean everything.

"At this point there aren't many people that would hold much against him. I think when he was younger, some people would.

"But now I think it is more a case of almost allowing him this happiness, and enjoying seeing him finish off the last days of his career in a place that makes him happy.

"So many people end their careers on a sour note, but for him he is going to be ending it doing exactly what he wants to do."

#857. Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?

The heat is on Australia as chief negotiator at the COP31 UN climate conference to forge a path away from coal and gas, and to protect Pacific neighbors facing rising sea levels.

In its role as president of negotiations at the UN climate talks in Turkey, Australia is being pressured to guide nations toward unified action on slashing the greenhouse gas emissions that are generated in large part by burning fossil fuels.

The nation has pledged to lead by example at the summit through a strong commitment to renewable energy, electrification and reduced reliance on planet-heating coal, oil and gas.

"Renewable energy, grids, storage and electrification are creating opportunities to strengthen resilience, improve energy security, and reduce emissions at the same time," said Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister, in October during a meeting in Fiji ahead of the COP climate conference.

"These are proven, commercial and scalable today. Now is the moment for faster implementation."

Yet Australia is also the world's third-largest exporter of fossil fuels. And unlike France and Germany, or island nations from Fiji to the Bahamas that are highly vulnerable to a changing climate, the COP31 co-president has not yet committed to phasing them out.

As calls grow for the country to set a clear route to a clean energy future, critics say its vague promise to transition away from polluting sources of power does not go far enough.

Australia is home to 56% of the world's coal mine projects currently in the pipeline, notes environmental nonprofit, 350.org.

Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at the organization, is calling on the country, the world's second-largest coal exporter, to reverse course and announce an "overdue coal phaseout date" during the COP31 conference.

"Australia needs to walk the walk and follow Germany's example and commit to a phaseout," said Melanie Pill, founder of The Climate Project, an Australia-based climate policy advisory.

The argument to end fossil fuel production is not only about cutting emissions but reducing dependence on energy systems that rely on volatile oil and gas markets, she explained.

"A fossil phaseout in the face of the enduring and escalating conflict in the Middle East is in the interest of everyone," Pill told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

This is especially true for Australia's diesel-reliant Pacific neighbors, who spend up to 25% of GDP on fossil fuel imports — as opposed 6% on health — according to a report by the Institute for Climate Risk and Response at the University of New South Wales.

As lead negotiator at the UN climate talks, Australia can "flip the narrative" on a fossil fuel phaseout, using the challenge of energy security as a justification, said Pill.

This opportunity could be lost, however, if Australia fails to address fossil fuel exports that accounted for 80% of its total carbon footprint in 2022 — and near 5% of global emissions.

While the nation is a world leader in rooftop solar, and generates around half of its electricity from renewables, this progress is "being undone by its continued approval of more fossil fuels for export," said Simon Bradshaw, COP31 lead and climate expert at Greenpeace Australia Pacific.

He noted that the Labor government of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has approved the construction, expansion or extension of 38 coal, oil and gas projects since coming to power four years ago on a pro-climate platform.

"You cannot aspire to lead on climate abroad if you're not getting your own house in order," said Thomas Houlie, climate and energy policy analyst at Climate Analytics, a global climate policy institute.

In 2025, when Australia approved the extension of a major gas export project in the country's west until 2070, Albanese justified the move in the name of a balance between "security of energy supply" and "support [for] the transition which reduces our emissions."

The country has publicly backed a global transition away from the fossil fuels driving the global temperature rise linked to extreme heat and drought. Both through the Global Stocktake agreed at the 2023 UN climate summit, and via the inaugural "transitioning away" summit in Colombia this April, at which Australia and 56 countries pledged to develop a fossil fuel exit road map.

But these commitments are not reflected in Australian resources policy, or its domestic rollout of clean power infrastructure.

"While the government has set a renewables target for electricity, it leaves plenty of blind spots in other sectors," said Houlie, adding that emission reductions in industry and transport have been limited and that the push to achieve an 82% renewables target for the electricity grid by 2030 is behind schedule.

In its role as lead negotiator at COP31, Australia has promised to ensure that any final conference text serves to "elevate the views and the experiences" of small Pacific nations in its region, from Vanuatu to Tuvalu.

These island countries that generate low emissions yet suffer extreme climate impacts from worsening cyclones or rising seas are "sick of Australia's double talk on climate," said Shiva Gounden, head of Pacific at Greenpeace Australia Pacific.

Australia must commit to "substantial new funding contributions" to help Pacific neighbors adapt to the climate emergency and achieve energy independence, said his colleague Bradshaw. He reiterated the need to concurrently create a "national road map" away from coal and gas production and export.

A Climate Analytics report co-authored by Houlie outlines a fossil fuel phaseout pathway for Australia that can begin immediately. This includes an end to coal power generation by 2034 and a rapid reduction in oil and gas consumption, with renewables generating almost all the country's electricity by 2040. Fossil fuel export projects would be eliminated, and existing ones shuttered before becoming obsolete.

"This co-presidency is a golden opportunity for Australia to step up and commit to a phaseout," said Houlie.

#856. Senegal and Morocco lead Afcon qualifiers but Tunisia protest

Senegal were stripped of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title by a Confederation of African Football appeals board, and are awaiting the outcome of their own appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport

Senegal became the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations before Cameroon and Morocco were among five others to join them with two games to spare - but there was penalty drama in Tripoli.

Tunisia, who have appeared at a record 17 consecutive editions of Afcon, are at risk of missing out after a contentious 1-1 draw against Libya.

Libya's penalty equaliser just before half-time followed protest scenes lasting over five minutes as players and staff from the Carthage Eagles challenged the decision.

The video assistant referee system is not used in Afcon qualifying, and Tunisia's remonstrating with the fourth official on the touchline ultimately only served to delay the spot-kick, which Ezoo El Mariamy, the player who was adjudged to have been fouled, converted.

Drawing the game meant Tunisia's winless start in Group H continued, with the Carthage Eagles having just three points from four games.

Tunisia need a strong finish to their campaign to give themselves a chance of reaching the finals, and Nigeria are also at risk of missing out, but others have made short order of qualifying.

Led by new head coach Patrick Vieira, Senegal moved to the brink of a place at the finals by beating Sudan 4-2 on Monday, and the Teranga Lions had their passage from Group J confirmed on Tuesday when Mozambique secured a 1-0 victory away against Ethiopia.

Cameroon and Benin also progressed without kicking a ball after Comoros and Burkina Faso registered wins - with the latter result also sealing a finals spot for the victorious Stallions.

Mali and Morocco extended their perfect starts and booked their places with triumphs over Rwanda and Niger respectively.

Abdellah Ouazane was the match-winner for Morocco in an away game that was actually played in Rabat, with the 17-year-old brilliantly curling in midway through the first half to cap a fine team move.

The Atlas Lions and Senegal are still waiting for the outcome of a case at the Court of Arbitration for Sport to decide the destination of the 2025 Afcon title.

Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time but Morocco were awarded the trophy by a Confederation of African Football appeals board which decreed the West Africans breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them.

Cameroon, Senegal and Benin close in on Afcon 2027 qualification

Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

Eleven sides had the chance to join co-hosts Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda at next year's finals when the fourth round of fixtures culminated on Tuesday.

Algeria, DR Congo, Egypt and the Ivorians all could have qualified with away wins but failed to pick up three points.

Brighton forward Yankuba Minteh was on target as The Gambia came from behind to lead Ivory Coast 2-1 in Group C, but Christ Inao Oulai grabbed an equaliser deep in stoppage time after Scorpions striker Muhammed Badamosi was sent off in the 90th minute.

Egypt were held to a goalless draw in Malawi, Sierra Leone claimed a late point against the Congolese and Algeria suffered a 3-0 defeat in Togo.

Angola beat South Sudan 1-0 in Juba and would have qualified had Egypt claimed victory in the other match in Group B.

Nigeria are in danger of failing to reach Afcon for the first time since 2017 after the Super Eagles failed to beat Tanzania.

The final two rounds of qualifiers will be held in March next year, with Afcon 2027 scheduled to be held in East Africa from 19 June to 17 July.

Malawi goalkeeper George Chikooka helped deny Mohamed Salah's Egypt an early passage to the Afcon 2027 finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda

Seven-time Afcon winners Egypt knew victory in Lilongwe could take them to the finals but were frustrated by an inspired second-half showing from Malawi goalkeeper George Chikooka.

After Pharaohs captain Mohamed Salah had hit the outside of the post from a tight angle, Chikooka denied Trezeguet and Haissem Hassan before also making fine stops from Mohamed Hany and Ibrahim Adel in stoppage time.

Egypt move on to eight points in Group B, two points behind Angola after Miro's first-half effort secured a 1-0 victory for the Palancas Negras in Juba.

There was drama as Ivory Coast salvaged a draw in Bakau through Inao Oulai's 98th-minute goal, which denied The Gambia a third win in Group C.

The Ivorians lead the pool on 10 points, with The Gambia on seven and Ghana on six following the Black Stars' back-to-back wins over Somalia.

DR Congo appeared on track to progress from Group E as Junior Kadile gave the Leopards a half-time lead in their away tie against Sierra Leone, but Alie Conteh netted in the 94th minute for the West Africans.

And Togo moved a point behind Group I leaders Algeria after a strong first-half showing in Lome, with two goals from Thibault Klidje before Kennedy Boateng's powerful header secured a 3-0 win over the 2019 champions from North Africa.

Eric Chelle's Nigeria failed to qualify for the 2026 Fifa World Cup and now face an uphill battle to reach Afcon 2027

Nigeria's hopes of progressing suffered another blow as Eric Chelle's men drew 0-0 with Tanzania in Zanzibar.

With East Africans Tanzania already assured of a spot at the finals, as co-hosts, Nigeria are competing with Guinea-Bissau for just one qualification spot available in Group L.

And Guinea-Bissau established a three-point advantage over the Super Eagles as goals from Mama Balde and Mauro Rodrigues gave them a 2-0 home win over Madagascar.

After falling to a 3-0 defeat in Bissau in September, even maximum points in the final two rounds of qualifiers may not be enough for three-time continental champions Nigeria to reach the tournament.

In another section with just one qualifying berth, Tunisia are in trouble at the foot of Group H on three points after the 1-1 draw with Libya in Tripoli.

Anis Ben Slimane capitalised on a defensive error to fire Tunisia ahead in the third minute, but El Mariamy levelled for the hosts from 12 yards in first-half injury time.

Tunisia's players and officials vehemently protested against the decision to award a foul after El Mariamy tussled with defender Ghaith Zaalouni and collided with goalkeeper Aymen Dahmen, delaying the penalty for several minutes.

The Tunisian visitors then had their own claims for a spot-kick turned down after a similar coming together between Mohamed Belhadj Mahmoud and Libya keeper Ayman Al Tihar, with players surrounding Beninois referee Adissa Ligali and his assistants at the full-time whistle.

The Carthage Eagles had also complained about refereeing decisions in the reverse fixture on Friday with a potential equaliser ruled out following a marginal offside call, before their North African neighbours sealed a 2-0 win.

Libya are one point behind Group H leaders Uganda after the Cranes drew 1-1 away against Botswana, who are one point better off than Tunisia.

Elsewhere, South Africa returned to the top of Group D with a 2-1 win over co-hosts Kenya, Cape Verde's chances of reaching the finals were hit by a 2-0 defeat in Liberia and Gabon suffered a shock 2-0 loss at the hands of Lesotho.

Benin, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Kenya (co-hosts), Mali, Morocco, Senegal, Tanzania (co-hosts), Uganda (co-hosts).

#855. Bachelor's Peter Weber Reveals He Married Pregnant Jadeyn Carr

Bachelor Nation alum Peter Weber and Jadeyn Carr privately tied the knot Nov. 11 while expecting their first child after hard-launching their relationship in August.

Peter Weber got his wish of finding a co-pilot for life.

The Bachelor star shared that he and Jadeyn Carr said "I do" in a private ceremony on Nov. 11, following the couple announcing their first pregnancy in September.

As the commercial flyer, nicknamed Pilot Pete, told fans aboard the Bachelor Nation cruise Nov. 17, "I can officially say that on 11/11, I married the love of my life."

The special gathering was made even more magical thanks to its unique wedding date, known for being a prime day to manifest big dreams coming true.

That said, keeping the conclusion of his journey to finding his final rose—which began on Hannah Brown’s season of The Bachelorette in 2019—under wraps was ultimately too exciting to withhold from his loyal fans any longer, as he revealed during a panel on the cruise.

"I was debating of revealing this here, but you guys have all been here, following my journey for a very long time," the Traitors alum explained. "I appreciate that, all the support."

While the 35-year-old, who hard-launched his relationship with the model in August, hasn't yet shared any further details about their nuptials, he did gush about the impending marriage in a cryptic post on their wedding day, when he shared an all-smiles selfie featuring Carr and her engagement ring with the caption, "Marry Me."

Following the affair, Golden Bachelor alum Renee Halverson-Wright gave some insight into the sweet occasion.

"It was the most beautiful, touching wedding ceremony," the 70-year-old replied to Bachelor Nation's Instagram, adding the celebration was "filled with so much love and exactly the way they both wanted it!"

And while the former reality star—who led season 24 of the ABC series in 2020—has kept much of their relationship private, his Aug. 13 carousel debuting their romance showed that his loved ones were already fans of his future bride. Case in point? Weber’s brother Jack Weber commented on his post, writing, "Love this," while his mom Barbara Weber wrote, "Happiness is…" alongside red heart emojis.

Following his time on The Bachelor, Weber dated Flanagan, who appeared on his season of the dating reality series. The two reunited in April 2020, but called it quits that following January. While he and Flanagan rekindled their romance in September 2022, he revealed they were no longer together in May 2023.

Will you accept this invitation to check in on the Bachelor's most memorable relationships? If so, read on...

Lest the couple forget where their journey began, they need only walk past the master bedroom in their Dallas-area pad. That's where the graphic designer has framed the final final rose that season 17's Bachelor presented her back in that Thai forest in late 2012, right after he promised to tell her he loved her every day of the rest of their lives.

"It made sense to dry this one and make it permanent because it was accompanied by a ring and a proposal, so this is a really special thing," Catherine explained to Entertainment Tonight in 2017. Because that last rose ceremony, complete with an elephant ride and a $75,000 Neil Lane diamond, is as much part of their story as the the sweet, suburban life that followed with kids Samuel, 5, Isaiah, 3, and Mia, 2. "We don't want to shy away from the fact that we got engaged and fell in love on The Bachelor," she said, "so that is the only red rose I will allow in my house!"

The OG Bachelorette, Trista was the first to prove that a stint in the mansion could lead to love, marriage and even Bachelor babies. "Nowadays they shoot the show for, I believe, three months. So it's like 12 weeks," the author shared with Us Weekly of her 2003 season. "My show was shot in six weeks. So Ryan and I met, got engaged, got married a year later, after knowing each other for six weeks. So that's how it used to be."Their decade years holding it down as the show's success story have taught the Colorado-based pair they can handle pretty much anything. Including months sheltering in place with their kids, son Maxwell, 14, and daughter Blakesley, 13. "It's really hard for us to get a date night. I think when the kids are working, we try to take advantage of that time as much as possible," she said of scheduling around the firefighter's early bird tendencies. "But yeah, we're good. We're 16 years and this too shall pass, as they say."

Who even remembers that the sweet divorced dad originally proposed to Melissa Rycroft? Okay, probably a lot of people, as his 2009 After the Final Rose switcheroo still ranks as one of the series' most shocking moments. But if all's well that end's well, the only thing that matters is that the Seattle-based parents to daughter Riley marked 10 years of marriage this past February. "Let me apologize publicly again for putting you through the Bachelor mess that I created," Jason, also dad to teen Ty, wrote in an anniversary tribute. "With that being said... it built an incredible, unique, foundation for us to build our family—showing that we can make it through anything."

In true Bachelor fashion, native Tennesseean Peyton simply knew when she laid eyes on her future husband. Though it wasn't season 10 lead Andy Baldwin. Nearly four years after the naval officer sent her home, the Bachelor Pad alum turned up at another series-related event in 2010 and spied Chris, fresh off his showing as Ali Fedotowsky's runner-up. "It's one of those things where I've had a ton of serious relationships," she later explained to People, "and I met this kid and he was genuine, outgoing and hilarious and we just click."By the following June, the landscaper was proposing at his home in Cape Cod. And more than a decade, two kids (daughter Lyla, 5, and son Hayes, 3) and a few HGTV and DIY Network shows later, they credit the series with laying their foundation. As Peyton put it in an August 2020 Instagram post, "Without the show I'm not sure our paths would have ever crossed."

For as much as the wedding dress designer seemed to key in on Brooks Forester during her 2013 season, it was sweet mortgage lender Chris and his thoughtful prose that proved to be the perfect fit. More than seven years after their L.A. vows (during which the Desiree Hartsock Bridal designer wore two of her own original creations) they're settled in Portland, Oregon, with sons Asher, 5, and Zander, 3. "If our life were a storybook I would be the damsel in distress," the host of podcast Heart of Purpose surmised in a February 2020 post. "Chris would be the funny yet charming knight who saves the day, Asher would be the pragmatic problem solver while his little brother would be the carefree sidekick trying to kiss all the ladies!" And they would all enjoy a happy ending. As Desiree put it in a post acknowledging the choice of Clare Crawley as Bachelorette, "Reality TV worked for me!"

The gold standard in Paradise success stories, the married duo have inspired countless rose seekers to turn up in Mexico with visions of Neil Lane diamonds and Chris Harrison-officiated vows dancing in their heads. The couple's time on the spin-off's second season yielded both, and with son Reed's November 2020 arrival, they'll tie the Lowes for most Bachelor offspring. "Life gets crazy sometimes," Jade wrote in a January anniversary post of juggling 4-year-old daughter Emmy and 2-year-old son Brooks, "but I wouldn't want to go through this hand-in-hand with anyone but you. I would choose you 1000 times over."

When the Bachelor in Paradise alum returned to the beaches of Nayarit, he was initially hesitant to pursue the Bachelor finalist, worried his peripatetic lifestyle wouldn't "mesh" with the former beauty queen's. But nearly three years (plus one brief breakup and a scary December 2019 ski accident that saw Dean laid up in Switzerland for weeks) later, they, and the van he calls home, are jelling just fine. "Obviously I was wrong about that because things are going well," he shared on his podcast Help! I Suck at Dating in October 2019, months before they started wearing rings to show their shared commitment. Mostly, he appreciates that she has a healthy level of snark and the ability to handle his jokes. "I can be myself around her," he continued. "Which is a nice change."

Though he skipped the Neil Lane-sponsored proposal on Bachelor in Paradise in 2018, Kevin was ready to take a knee by the following fall, proposing in his native Toronto where he and Astrid share a home. While they've since had to push off their planned November 2020 vows in her Florida hometown, "We're actually okay with it," Astrid wrote on Instagram, noting that making the decision to postpone due to the coronavirus pandemic allowed them to focus on their connection more than the myriad wedding details. "I wouldn't want to tackle 2020 & the rest of life with anyone else by my side." Now "back in the full swing of wedding planning," as she put it on Instagram, they'll wed this October just weeks before son August's first birthday.

Even the most wishful of Bachelorette fans likely weren't betting on JoJo and Jordan's journey leading them to an altar. Because with the persistent rumors of the former Vanderbilt quarterback's ill intentions ramping up even before they took the stage for the requisite grin-and-gush After the Final Rose appearance in 2016, it seemed unlikely she would still be wearing her 3.75-carat Neil Lane diamond years later.Which, she's not. But only because Jordan presented the real estate developer with an upgrade in August 2019. Though their summer 2020 wedding plans were scrapped due to the pandemic ("I know it will be all more worth the wait," JoJo wrote in a post acknowledging their would-be June day), they tied the knot in May 2022. "You make me laugh, love me endlessly, encourage me to be brave, and always, without fail, are my biggest cheerleader," the native Texan wrote in a post on their fourth anniversary. "Can't wait for what the rest of our lives have in store for us."

Consider Ashley the poster child for ignoring all of the standard he's-just-not-that-into-you signs. Because after four years of lusting for the guy she declared her dream man upon sight, she was proven right at their August 2019 vows in Newport, R.I. Every bit as all-in as his bride, who welcomed their son Dawson in January, Jared reflected on their perfect day on Instagram, writing, "Ashley is my best friend, my person, my soulmate and now my wife. I love this woman more than words will ever allow me to express."

Who needs Neil Lane and a beach backdrop when you have this much imagination? The Dallas-based real estate agent went big when proposing to his Paradise love in May 2019. "She thought it was a normal shoot day," Adam told E! News of his plan to turn a set-up for her online boutique into an impromptu engagement session. "We were at the helicopter pad on the roof and Raven had roses in her hand. She was throwing the petals up for cute photos. She did a few practice runs and then the videographer slipped me the ring and once she threw the petals up, I got down on one knee. I blacked out, but I got everything out that I wanted."

Three months after their April 2021 vows, she announced she was expecting son Gates. "OVER THE MOON EXCITED TO SHARE THE NEWS!" she wrote on social media. "I've loved you before you were in my womb!" Raven and Adam welcomed the child in January 2022.

Sure, she waffled a bit in the early days of Paradise, unsure if her heart belonged to Barbour or Blake Horstmann, but once she zeroed in on the tech entrepreneur, she truly committed. Now the California-based duo are busying themselves with putting together their dream nuptials. While Barbour is set on a good DJ and "maybe an In-N-Out truck," Godwin is thinking big picture. "I have a few little things saved on social media," she told E! News in November 2019. "I have such fun ideas, but good weather, a cool view and a really good time. That's the one thing we do talk about and reiterate."

So he pulled a Mesnick? More than three years after Bachelor Arie dumped onetime fiancée Becca Kufrin on-air to start things up again with Lauren, the pair are married (Chris Harrison officiated their January 2019 wedding in Hawaii, natch), loving life with their 2-year-old daughter Alessi and 11-month-old twins Lux and Senna and perfecting the art of getting through tough times together. Following a heartbreaking 2020 miscarriage, Arie gifted his bride with an eternity band symbolizing "that we will always have each other in our darkest times," Lauren explained. "i think it's safe to say he gets husband of the year." To hear Arie tell it, though, makes him the lucky one. "The fact is, I'm really happy with Lauren," he told GQ in 2018 of their origin story. "So for me, it was all worth it."
